cases.statement: One carrier: Case 1, a 58-year-old Chinese woman (heterozygous) with adult-onset AxD resembling a parkinsonian/MSA-like syndrome.

people.label: Case 1
people.key_phenotypes: 5-year progressive gait disturbance and lower-limb weakness; dysarthria, dysphagia, constipation, urinary incontinence; left-gaze nystagmus and left cerebellar signs; mild cognitive impairment (MoCA 20/30); medulla oblongata atrophy and upper cervical cord thinning with supratentorial white-matter changes

quotes.quote: A 58-year-old woman presented with a 5-year history of progressive gait disturbance and lower-limb weakness.

Her key associated features were dysarthria, hypophonic speech, dysphagia with choking on liquids, constipation, urinary incontinence, episodic dizziness, rapid eye movement (REM) sleep-related abnormal behaviors, anxiety, depression, and recent short-term memory decline.
Neurological examination showed dysarthria, mild cognitive impairment, left-gaze nystagmus, and left-sided cerebellar impairment.
Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed marked atrophy of the medulla oblongata and thinning of the upper cervical spinal cord, as well as supratentorial white-matter changes (Figure 1a–d).
| Cognitive Status (MoCA) | 20/30 (mild impairment) | 29/30 (preserved) | 18/30 (significant impairment) | Mild subjective decline |

phenotype_specificity.statement: Adult-onset pattern with cervicomedullary atrophy; earlier diagnosed as a parkinsonian syndrome; autonomic testing showed sympathetic dysfunction. Single-proband whole-exome sequencing; whether other genes or other variants were considered is not reported.

quotes.quote: She had previously been diagnosed with a parkinsonian syndrome.
Autonomic testing showed reduced sympathetic skin response amplitudes, indicating sympathetic dysfunction.
peripheral-blood genomic DNA was analyzed by single-proband capture-based high-throughput whole-exome sequencing.

segregation.statement: No relatives tested; three-generation family history negative.

quotes.quote: A three-generation family history was obtained, and no family history of similar neurological symptoms or known neurodegenerative disease was reported.
No Sanger confirmation or trio-based analysis was documented in the available report.

de_novo.statement: Parents not tested (no trio analysis documented); de novo status unknown.

quotes.quote: No Sanger confirmation or trio-based analysis was documented in the available report.

functional.statement: No variant-specific functional study; the paper says so explicitly.

quotes.quote: Variant-specific functional studies were not available for the GFAP variants identified in our cases; therefore, their precise molecular effects cannot be directly inferred.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: In-frame deletion of 9 nucleotides removing three residues, p.(Glu122_Arg124del), in exon 1. The paper gives a general mechanism (mutant GFAP aggregation; non-hotspot variants may disrupt filament assembly) but nothing specific to this variant.

quotes.quote: even non-hotspot variants might disrupt filament assembly, reduce solubility, and promote aggregation [25].
In experimental settings, it was found that mutant GFAP accumulates in non-soluble components, forms aggregates with ubiquitin and small heat-shock proteins, and activates stress-response mechanisms

authors_classification.statement: Variant of uncertain significance by ACMG, with PM2 and PM4.

quotes.quote: located in exon 1 and classified as a variant of uncertain significance according to ACMG criteria, with supporting evidence PM2 and PM4.
| Pathogenicity (ACMG) | VUS | VUS (co-segregation noted) | Likely pathogenic | VUS |

concerns: The variant was not confirmed by Sanger sequencing (none documented) and no relative was tested.
The authors cite the population criterion they used but the paper gives no population database or frequency.
Case series; the paper notes the variant interpretation was 'conservative' and combined with clinical and MRI features.
notes_for_panel: Single adult case, no confirmation, segregation or functional data.
